title: Phantom stock after an auto-receipt
brief: Store replenishment orders for SKU P-420 (pan set) from the Madrid DC are shipping short, although the system shows 900 units in stock. Find the root cause and an action plan.

evidence.content: WMS shows 900 P-420 on hand in Madrid, all in bin 12-B.
Pickers raised 'empty bin' exceptions for P-420 on 14 of 20 picks this week. Bin 12-B is physically empty.
The last P-420 receipt was ASN 7781 on 22 Oct: 900 units booked into Madrid by ASN auto-receipt (no physical count at the dock).
Proof of delivery for ASN 7781 shows 0 pallets delivered to Madrid: the truck was rerouted to the Valencia DC on 22 Oct because of dock congestion.
The supplier invoiced 900 units of P-420 shipped on 20 Oct.
Store demand for P-420 is in line with forecast.
Valencia DC reports 900 unidentified P-420 units received on 23 Oct, sitting in quarantine because no ASN matched them.

answer_key.root_cause: ASN auto-receipt booked 900 P-420 units into Madrid that were physically delivered to Valencia (rerouted truck), creating phantom stock in Madrid; the real units sit in quarantine in Valencia.

remediation_rubric.criterion: Transfer the quarantined units from Valencia to Madrid
Correct Madrid's inventory record (cycle count / adjustment)
Stop auto-receipt without physical confirmation, or reconcile ASNs with proof of delivery
Make carriers notify reroutes to the receiving DC

answer_key.notes: E7 arrives late and confirms where the stock went.

registry.mechanism_opportunities: V1: Logistics -> Inventory findings are central. V3: E4 contradicts the receipt booked in E3. E7 (round 3) adds where the stock went.
registry.expected_timing: Cause clear from round 2; E7 in round 3 completes the action plan.
registry.favoritism_notes: E7 rewards teams that keep going after a plausible answer.
